headline: Ramayana's Five-Language Run Puts Yash on the Verge of a Box-Office First
subheadline: KGF Chapter 2 crossed ₹50 crore in all five major languages in 2022. Ramayana is completing the same sweep, which would make Yash the only actor to headline two such films — one Kannada, one Hindi.
body:
• Trade tracker Sacnilk's day-15 tally has Ramayana past ₹50 crore gross in Hindi, Kannada and Telugu, with Tamil (₹48 crore) and Malayalam (₹47.6 crore) within about ₹2 crore of the mark; Koimoi reports the five-language sweep already complete.
  • KGF Chapter 2 crossed ₹50 crore in each of the five languages in 2022, so Yash is set to become the only actor to headline two films on the all-five list — one Kannada, one Hindi.
  • Ramayana has reached ₹1,547.15 crore worldwide in 15 days, according to Sacnilk, passing KGF Chapter 2's lifetime worldwide gross of ₹1,215 crore.
  • The film's dubbed versions alone have crossed ₹200 crore net in India, a first for a Bollywood film, according to Koimoi.

Ramayana: Part 1, the Hindi-language epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari, is completing a box-office sweep no Bollywood film has managed before: ₹50 crore or more in gross collections in every one of India's five major film languages. For Yash, who plays Ravana opposite Ranbir Kapoor's Ram, the milestone carries a personal record — he already headlined one of the only two films ever to do it, the Kannada blockbuster KGF Chapter 2.

Where the numbers stand

"On Sacnilk's language-version tally, only two films have ever crossed ₹50 crore in each of the five versions: KGF Chapter 2 and Rishab Shetty's Kantara Chapter 1."

Trade tracker Sacnilk's language-by-language tally through day 15 has Ramayana past ₹50 crore gross in Hindi (₹789.05 crore), Kannada (₹84.13 crore) and Telugu (₹63.37 crore), with Tamil at ₹48 crore and Malayalam at ₹47.60 crore — each within roughly ₹2 crore of the benchmark, with the third weekend expected to close the gap. Koimoi, the other major trade tracker, reports the sweep as already complete after 15 days. The two trackers' estimates differ slightly, but both put the film at worst days away from the mark in all five languages.

KGF Chapter 2's lifetime language grosses show the scale of what Ramayana is matching: ₹487.56 crore in Hindi, ₹170.77 crore in Kannada, ₹132.02 crore in Telugu, ₹114.94 crore in Tamil and ₹55.94 crore in Malayalam. Ramayana's Hindi gross alone has already far passed that film's, while its southern versions are doing the quieter, rarer work.

A two-film club of one

On Sacnilk's language-version tally, only two films have ever crossed ₹50 crore in each of the five versions: KGF Chapter 2 and Rishab Shetty's Kantara Chapter 1. Shetty has one such film; Yash is set to have two — and his pair spans two different industries: a Kannada film built around him, and a Hindi epic in which he plays the antagonist. That cross-industry span is what makes the record his alone, and Ramayana is the first Bollywood production to reach the benchmark.

The dubbed-version numbers underline it. Ramayana's four dubbed versions — Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam — have together crossed ₹206 crore net in India, making it the first Bollywood film to enter the ₹200 crore club on dubbed versions alone, according to Koimoi; the previous record holder, Adipurush, collected ₹137.50 crore from its dubbed versions. Worldwide, the film has reached ₹1,547.15 crore in 15 days on Sacnilk's tally — past ₹1,500 crore in its second week and beyond KGF Chapter 2's lifetime worldwide gross of ₹1,215 crore.

The film and how to watch it

Ramayana: Part 1 is a Hindi-language retelling of the Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi, with dubbed versions in Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam. It is in its third week in cinemas in India and overseas — its overseas gross stands at ₹515 crore on Sacnilk's tally — and its Kerala run has already made it the first Bollywood film to cross ₹50 crore in that state. No streaming date has been announced; for now, the five-language record is being written entirely at the box office.

key_takeaways: Ramayana grossed over ₹50 crore in Hindi, Kannada, and Telugu.
Yash is set to headline two films grossing ₹50 crore in all five languages.
Ramayana surpassed KGF Chapter 2's worldwide gross in just 15 days.
The film's dubbed versions have crossed ₹200 crore net in India.
Ramayana is the first Bollywood film to achieve this five-language milestone.
